title: Agent latency evidence record
description: One agent task run, measured so that model time, tool time, local-command time and resource waiting stay separable, and so that the quality of the result is recorded next to its duration. S2760. A cost or context figure is never a latency figure and never a quality figure: this schema has no field that accepts one, and a record that reports a saved token count in place of a measured duration is invalid by construction.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this record shape. Bumped when a field changes meaning, never when a field is added.

recordId.description: Stable identifier of this run, unique inside the ticket's evidence directory.

date.description: Absolute date of the run, YYYY-MM-DD. Relative wording does not survive the comparison it feeds.

ticket.description: Ticket the run was performed under, when it had one.

taskClass.description: Owner-named class of work. The three classes are the control set: mechanical or script work, code search and research, Kotlin development and build.

controlTaskId.description: Identifier of the control task. Two records may only be compared when this value matches, because a duration without a fixed task measures the task, not the route.

routeId.description: The route under test: which model, which reasoning effort, inline or subagent, and any verbosity setting, spelled out enough to be reproduced.

routeSettings.description: The individual settings behind routeId, so a later reader can tell which lever moved.

firstResponseMs.description: Client-observed milliseconds from submitting the request to the first visible output token. Not measurable by any repository script - it is supplied by the operator from the client.

modelDurationMs.description: Client-observed milliseconds the model spent reasoning and emitting output, when the client exposes it. Frequently unavailable, which is why it is optional and why 'unavailable' must carry a reason.

toolDurationMs.description: Milliseconds spent inside tool and local-command execution - gradle, gates, scripts, greps. Repository-observed and measured monotonically.

queueWaitMs.description: Milliseconds spent waiting for a resource rather than working: a build or code domain lock, a ticket lease, a queued sibling session. Repository-observed. Zero is a real measurement and must be written as zero, never omitted.

totalCompletionMs.description: Milliseconds from request to the finished, accepted result. This is the number the owner feels; the stages above explain where it went.

qualityVerdict.description: Whether the run produced the accepted result. 'incomplete' means the route did not finish the task and disqualifies it regardless of its durations.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The criteria the result was judged against. Compared routes must carry an identical set, or the comparison measures two different tasks.

validationEvidence.description: Each mandatory check that was run, with its exit code or PASS/FAIL. An empty list is not allowed: a run with no evidence has no verdict to compare.

reworkCount.description: Number of fix iterations needed after the first result was presented. A faster route that needs a second pass is not faster.

notes.description: Free operator remarks. Never a substitute for a measurement or an unavailable-metric reason.

measurement.description: A measured duration, or an explicit statement that it could not be measured together with the reason it could not. There is no third form: an absent metric with no reason silently reads as zero in every later average, which is the failure this shape exists to prevent.

source.description: Who observed it. A client-observed field may not be filled in by a repository script, and a repository-observed field may not be typed in from a feeling.

unavailableReason.description: Why this stage could not be measured on this run - for example the client exposes no reasoning duration.
